set.body:
Raised by independent review at the start of Epic 4, while R/compiler.R is still untouched.

Process observation

Epic 4 declares deps: Epic 0A (blocks), Epic 2 (blocks), Epic 3 (blocks). Epic 2 and 3 are closed; Epic 0A is still open. mote ready confirms it - Epic 4 does not appear in the ready list, Epic 0A does. Epic 4 was claimed anyway.

Why the ordering is substantive, not bureaucratic

Epic 4 acceptance includes: "Plan identity records scientific semantics; execution receipt records the actual lowering, blocks, cache behavior, and materialization."

That criterion is currently UNFALSIFIABLE, because the lowering cannot vary through any public path:

- geometry() and evaluate_geometry() (compiler.R:761, 776) accept no normalizer, transform, or reducer.
- .run_geometry_compiler() does not take them either.
- .compiler_plan_id() (compiler.R:409-411) carries normalizer = inner_product(), transform = NULL, reducer = .partition_reducer() as DEFAULTS ONLY, and .run_geometry_compiler never passes anything else.
- The receipt at compiler.R:690-699 hardcodes exactly those same three values plus lowering = "bilinear".

So the receipt and the plan agree today only because both are pinned to one possible value. No test can distinguish "the receipt is read from the executed plan" from "the receipt is a constant that happens to match", because there is exactly one plan.

The only things that could make the lowering vary are the edge-operation constructors - correlation(), cosine(), covariance(), fisher_z(), rank_edges(), inner_product(), aggregate_first(), reduce_partitions() - and their evaluator .evaluate_edge_operation(). Those are precisely the exports Epic 0A must either wire into a public workflow or delete. Until that decision is made, Epic 4 cannot demonstrate its central claim, and its plan and receipt schemas will be designed around vocabulary that Epic 0A may remove.

Baseline confirmed unchanged as of this pass (R/compiler.R mtime 22:24 yesterday):
- .compile_effect_task has exactly ONE call site in R/, at compiler.R:412, inside .compiler_plan_id, whose entire return value is a digest string. The compiled task is still built and discarded.
- The receipt edge_operation block at compiler.R:690-699 is still a literal.

Suggested sequencing

Resolve Epic 0A first, or at minimum make its decision before Epic 4 freezes the plan/receipt schema. If the edge calculus is retained, Epic 4 gains a testable acceptance criterion for free: construct two plans differing only in normalizer or transform and assert the receipts differ and the numbers differ accordingly. If the calculus is deleted, Epic 4 should drop normalizer/transform/reducer from plan identity rather than carry dead fields into the new schema.

Either way, Epic 4 should not close on a receipt criterion that no test can currently fail.
set.title: Epic 4 claimed with Epic 0A open; its receipt acceptance is unfalsifiable until the edge calculus is resolved
